overview: White declines the gambit with 2.d5, gaining space and a Benoni-like wedge. Black replies ...Bd6, ...f5 or ...Nf6 and tries to undermine d5 or play on the kingside. No pawn is given up, so it is a space game for White and a counter for Black.

white_ideas.idea: Hold the d5 wedge with c4, Nc3, e4 and gain space
Develop Nf3, Nc3 and play for a slight advantage

typical_structures.structure: d5 against e5 (Old Benoni or Czech Benoni-like)

character.notes: Quiet space game; unclear and little theory.

gambit.notes: No material changes hands in the declined line.

soundness.notes: White's 2.d5 is playable; nothing is refuted.

structure.notes: Pawns on d5/e5 and the centre not yet fixed; can become Benoni-like or closed.

approach.notes: A seldom-chosen way to meet the Englund; most White players take the pawn.

level.notes: Few moves to learn; space and pawn breaks need judgement.

character.reason: Quiet space game with no forcing lines.

gambit.reason: Declined; no material is given up.

structure.reason: Centre unresolved; could lock to closed.

approach.reason: A rare reply seldom seen among strong players.

level.reason: Little to memorise but plans need judgement.
